title: Density geometry on neurOS and EEG foundation-model representations
objective: Test whether trace-one PSD latent geometry adds reproducible longitudinal, cross-subject, or calibration value beyond complexity-matched classical geometry on identical neurOS/foundation representations and frozen evidence authority.
decision_gates: Primary longitudinal lanes must consume neurOS GroupedEvaluationData plus serialized neurOS partition/calibration authority; QuantumBCI may not silently re-split those samples.
No subject or session may appear in both train and final evaluation partitions; target calibration examples must remain disjoint from the fixed final evaluation set.
The scientific run identity must bind the upstream raw-data fingerprint, neurOS partition fingerprint, neurOS nested-calibration fingerprint, QuantumBCI source revision, and neurOS source revision.
Foundation-model execution must inherit neurOS fail-closed adapter semantics; unavailable upstream models may not be replaced by mock or random embeddings in benchmark evidence.
The density representation must be compared against covariance/tangent-space, bilinear Gram, PCA, random-PSD, and identical-dimensional readout controls on the exact same embedding tensors.

Promotion requires a paired subject-level 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero against the strongest matched control on at least two datasets or paradigms, plus an absolute >=0.01 macro-F1/balanced-accuracy gain OR a >=0.02 absolute calibration improvement.
Off-diagonal removal must measurably reduce any claimed density-specific benefit; otherwise the result is representation compression, not evidence for a coherence-like mechanism.
Observables used in the interpretation must be stable across seeds and subject bootstrap resamples before they enter the mechanism ledger.
